DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 90 s. 2022 14 September 2022 HON. CEASAR C. SORIANO Mayor, Municipality of Siocon Zamboanga del Norte Dear Mayor Soriano: This has reference to your letter dated July 1 1, 2022 requesting the DILG Secretary to approve your proposal to engage in a TV where you can showcase the counter- insurgency efforts of the Municipality of Siocon by featuring your best practices and that of nearby municipalities with the end view of addressing the terrorist attacks in the locality. To bolster this, you stated in your aforesaid letter-request: "As the incumbent Mayor of Siocon, I believe that it is my responsibility to usher-in a new future for our town-one filled with hope, peace and progress. By volunteering for this noble purpose, I can set a good example to my fellow Sioconians by providing them with a clear vision of true development and peace through TV features, public service announcements, and the needed information to effectively respond to any conflicts and disasters. This will be done only for one- hour every Sunday on PTV4." In this regard, please be informed that a TV Program Engagement, insofar as it will virtuously put forward the counter-insurgency measures of the local government, will contribute in disseminating counter-insurgency information and campaign. Thus, the same fall within the powers of local government units provided under the general welfare provision of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, viz: "SECTION 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied there from, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants." (Emphasis Supplied) In the light of it being a public function within the ambit of the general welfare clause, the Department resolves that approval of the Department for the contemplated TV Program Engagement is not necessary. This is in correlation to the constitutionally "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

guaranteed principle of local autonomy which assures local governments' discretion in carrying out their obligations and functions. Nonetheless, it is understood that in the event of involvement of utilization of government funds for the said TV Program, such as in the procurement of television airtime for said anti-insurgency TV program/segment, R.A. No. 9184, othenn.'ise known as the "Government Procurement Reform Act" and its Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations apply. Notwithstanding the foregoing opinion, however, if the TV Program Engagement is in the nature of an occupation such that the Mayor will be compensated and the engagement is on a regular basis that will devote official time of the concerned Mayor, this level's opinion is in the negative. We anchor our position on the prohibition expressly provided by Section 90 of the Local Government Code, viz: "Sec. 90. Practice of Profession. — (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives." Conformably, as cited and discussed in the case of Javellana vs. DILG and Sec. Luis T. Santosl and in a long line of !ega! opinions rendered by the Department, Provincia! Governors, City and Municipal Mayors whose duties and responsibilities require that their entire time be at the disposal of the government are prohibited to engage in the practice of their profession and to accept private employment during their incumbency. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
